quoted_tweet.text:
Agent platform of 2027. 

This is the end game. This is the blueprint for the one and only application layer software that will exist. Every other software will effectively become databases for this layer, the everything agentic operating system for the million agent swarm to work on top of. 

This is obviously the end game vision for the application layer of ChatGPT and Claude. I have reasons to believe that an independent company will own this product layer. But most ADE, "enterprise agent platform", or vertical saas companies, are focused on the wrong things far too narrowly, not technically competent, and do not have the product / technical vision to see this inevitable future. 

The correct agent platform that wins will function like the base of a garden, from which customers will plant their unique "seeds" to grow their own plants and trees, managed and evolved by agents, humans, and signals from the sensors of the business. This presents a clearer picture than "factory of a factory" imo.

text:
Summarizing memories throws details away.

MIRIX-2.0, from the MIRIX AI team, keeps every record word for word instead. Their example: Mia tells her assistant she got a Suica card, then weeks later asks how to get around Tokyo. An assistant without memory tells her to go buy one.

Storage is split across six agents. Each one owns a single kind of memory, like events, facts or skills.

Above the records sits a map of people, places and events. Every link on it points back to the exact record it came from, so the map never stands in for what was actually said.

Retrieval starts at a node. Mia asks about Tokyo, the system begins at her name on the map, reads a handful of linked records, and answers that she already has the card. That handful stays the same size however long her history gets.

Between conversations it runs an offline pass called AutoDream.

here's what AutoDream does 👇
→ merges names that mean the same thing, like "steel bottle" and "stainless steel bottle"
→ turns finished tasks into skills it can reuse later
→ leaves every stored record untouched

On LongMemEval-S it scores 72.6%, 14.3 points above the strongest baseline. On MetaClaw-Bench, which tests skill memory, it reaches 49.2% against 44.0% for MetaClaw's own skill library.

It also posts the highest mean success rate of the compared memory methods on both ALFWorld and WebShop.

The first MIRIX paper came out in July 2025 with eight agents across six memory components, and its code is on GitHub under Mirix-AI.
We’re all getting more dependent on this day after day

quoted_tweet.author: Superman
quoted_tweet.text:
Researchers discovered a new psychological condition caused by ChatGPT.

They're calling it "Cognitive Surrender."

Researchers ran three experiments across 1,372 people and 9,593 reasoning trials. They gave participants access to an AI assistant, but secretly rigged the AI to be accurate on some trials and subtly wrong on others.

People consulted the AI on more than 50% of the trials.

When the AI was right, human accuracy jumped by 25 percentage points.

When the AI was wrong, accuracy crashed by 15 percentage points.

Participants didn't double-check the output. They didn't catch the errors. They let System 3 override both their gut instinct and their critical thinking.

Then came the darker finding.

Using the AI made people measurably more confident in their answers—even when the AI fed them completely wrong information.

The researchers tried to break the habit. They added time pressure. They gave participants live feedback and financial incentives to get the right answer.

It didn't work.

Even when money was on the line, people still surrendered their judgment to a faulty AI.

We used to think AI was just a tool to help us think faster.

It's not. It's quietly replacing the act of thinking altogether.

quoted_tweet.author: Riley Brown
quoted_tweet.text:
finally taking the time to learn t3code. 

tried 2 months ago and was too... "developery"

Let's just say... i did not realize how far along this product is. 

I was reluctant to try it, because I use artifacts quite often for writing and content workflows... and to my surprise claude artifacts work quite well inside t3code. 

in fact you can open them in the t3code browser (i didn't know they had this)... 

And then i went to connect the iOS app. I didn't even have to scan a qr code... it just kinda... connected. THEN i realized you can control the t3code browser from your phone. wtf. 

Anyway, as many of u know i've been obsessed with creating content workflows for the past few months...
And if there's one thing i've learned over that time is the OpenAI models, the Claude Models, and the Gemini models all have their own strengths and weaknesses.

For instance gemini is really good at video understanding (taking a video, analyzing the different elements of a video from visuals, to sound etc), and Claude is really good at actually writing the code to edit the video.

Well, w t3 you can just have claude spin up a gemini subagent that analyzes 20+ videos and provide a report back to claude to actually do the edits. 

Additionally, when editing shorts you can basically have Neon, Astra, and Fable all attempt to edit the same video from the same context, all from a single prompt. This makes doing different types of creative workflow evals much easier. 

Bravo Theo, this is a great tool... However, it's just a little too expensive for my liking.
